key_insight: A realistically bent silicon crystalline undulator can generate a distinct, high-brilliance MeV gamma-ray peak using a 10 GeV positron beam, with the target undulator signal clearly separated from channeling background.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that FEM-informed structural deformation modeling can guide compact gamma-ray source design with performance competitive with large-scale facilities and superior to inverse-Compton scattering sources.
method: FEM simulated the bending profile of a patterned Si$_3$N$_4$-stressed Si(110) crystal
Relativistic molecular dynamics (MBN Explorer) tracked 10 GeV positron motion and photon emission
Emission probability and brilliance were evaluated for realistic aperture settings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an undulator radiation peak at 1.6–2.1 MeV and a maximum peak brilliance of about 5×10^22 photons/s/mm^2/mrad^2/0.1% BW at an optimal aperture of 1/2γ.
watch_item: Performance depends on realistic fabrication, stressor uniformity, and precise crystal bending; deviations could broaden the peak or reduce brilliance.
paper_title: High-Intense Gamma-Ray Emission from a Crystalline Undulator with Realistic Bending Profiles
